reason: Retain the certified base-domain mechanism as research opt-in. F2 preserves a certificate advantage over censored P but is materially slower than ENS and contemporary J. N2 improves ENS while losing to P; C2 loses both references at late common budgets, and C3 loses ENS upper bound. Frozen V30 and F5 confirm actual material budget gains against both references, while frozen V50 materially regresses against ENS on both upper bound and gap. No severe certification-time regression is observed; all new confirmation/long arms are unproved and eventual certification rankings remain unknown. This mixed finite panel does not justify replacing the protected default or a claim of stable complete-solve improvement. It also does not establish universal weakness of the inherited necessary hull or pure-cut causality.
